verdict.rationale: Restate lets developers write handlers as ordinary code through first-party SDKs for TypeScript, Java/Kotlin, Python, Go and Rust. `ctx.run` wraps any operation and stores its result in the execution log, so completed steps are checkpointed and execution resumes from where it left off after failures. A community user also reports getting an existing app running with the TS SDK. Missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement contrasting this with YAML/DSL definitions (it is only implied by the SDK model), and independent hands-on corroboration of step checkpointing and recovery.

support.subject: As a backend developer, I write workflows as ordinary code in my language — steps with automatic checkpointing — not YAML or a proprietary DSL

citations.quote: Code automatically stores completed steps and resumes from where it left off when recovering from failures.
Use `ctx.run` to safely wrap any non-deterministic operation, like HTTP calls or database responses, and have Restate store its result in the execution log.
Restate supports the following SDKs: * [Typescript] * [Java and Kotlin] * [Python] * [Go] * [Rust]
Chain agentic and traditional steps in sequence. Each step is recorded for automatic recovery.
I used it for an existing app + restate TS sdk, really took a few steps to get things up and running!
